question: You need to give medications to two patients in your ward. What should you do with your equipment?

options.A: Rinse the syringe with hot water between patients
options.B: Change only the needle and keep the same syringe barrel
options.C: Use the same syringe if the drug is prescribed for both
options.D: Use a fresh, sterile syringe and needle for each patient

explanation: Syringes and needles are strictly single-use. Never share them between patients—ever! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h3)

question: How does linking daily unit goals to the bigger hospital mission help frontline nurses?

options.A: It isolates them from the rest of the healthcare team.
options.B: It gives them a sense of purpose by connecting daily work to the wider mission.
options.C: It forces them to perform administrative duties instead of patient care.
options.D: It decreases their responsibility for patient safety outcomes.

explanation: It feels great to know that your busy shift on the ward is actually part of something much bigger and meaningful for patient care! [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient recovering from an intentional overdose is now awake and stable. What nursing action is most important?

options.A: Restricting all family visits to punish the patient for the suicide attempt
options.B: Providing continuous observation and psychological support while keeping the environment safe
options.C: Avoiding any conversation about the incident to prevent embarrassment
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately with a prescription for sedatives

explanation: You've got this. Emotional support and a safe, watch-careful environment are vital for anyone recovering from self-harm. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why does the body's immune system attack mismatched blood?

options.A: It tries to repair the damaged cells using white blood cells
options.B: It recognizes the foreign antigens as nonself and makes antibodies
options.C: It runs out of normal plasma proteins to handle the extra fluid
options.D: It mistakes the red blood cells for harmful bacteria

explanation: You've got this! The immune system's main job is spotting foreign invaders. When it sees unfamiliar antigens on donated red blood cells, it treats them as dangerous and attacks. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why must nurses change bed linens with extra care during Gallows traction?

options.A: To stop the baby from rolling onto their stomach
options.B: To keep the fracture and traction setup perfectly aligned
options.C: To keep the weights from breaking
options.D: To save money on hospital laundry

explanation: Any sudden shake can disturb the healing bone and cause great pain. Smooth, careful movements are key! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h4)

question: How often should you check the medication insertion site of a syringe driver?

options.A: Only when an alarm starts beeping
options.B: Only once every seven days
options.C: At least every nursing shift
options.D: Every time the patient falls asleep

explanation: Correct! Checking the site every shift helps you spot early redness, swelling, or irritation before it becomes a big problem for your patient. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the main thing that makes a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) different in healthcare?

options.A: Generating high profits for private shareholders
options.B: Operating independently outside direct government control
options.C: Replacing all national health ministries completely
options.D: Providing only curative hospital-based surgeries

explanation: NGOs stand out because they operate separately from government structures. This freedom lets them move quickly and help out right where communities need them most! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T27#GNS225_U5_T27_h1)

question: Which factor is a common logistical barrier to emergency referrals in rural communities?

options.A: An excessive surplus of functional ambulances
options.B: Poor road networks and lack of reliable transport
options.C: Too many specialists working in primary health posts
options.D: Free fuel supplies provided by local youth groups

explanation: Bad roads and lack of vehicles often delay the physical transfer of emergency patients to higher facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: How does compact bone contribute to movement?

options.A: By transmitting nerve impulses directly to muscle cells
options.B: By producing lubricating fluid for smooth joint movement
options.C: By acting as rigid levers that skeletal muscles pull against
options.D: By contracting actively alongside surrounding muscle fibers

explanation: Bones act as hard levers, allowing skeletal muscles to create coordinated body movement across joints. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is a common sign that prompts a patient to suspect they might have a tapeworm?

options.A: Passing flat, white worm segments in the stool
options.B: Coughing up blood-stained sputum during the night
options.C: Noticing painful swelling in the lower limbs
options.D: Developing severe jaundice in the eyes and skin

explanation: Spot on! Patients often notice moving or detached worm segments (proglottids) in their toilet visits, which is usually what brings them to the clinic. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h4)

question: What is the main action of mifepristone in the body?

options.A: It prevents infection by suppressing the immune system
options.B: It stimulates strong, rhythmic uterine contractions
options.C: It directly softens the cervix by increasing estrogen
options.D: It acts as a progesterone receptor antagonist

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the key hormone that keeps the uterine lining thick and secure during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h1)

question: What is an example of secondary prevention when caring for vulnerable families?

options.A: Punishing parents who miss immunizations
options.B: Screening for early signs of disease like malnutrition or high blood pressure
options.C: Treating severe late-stage illnesses in the ICU
options.D: Building brand new clinics in remote towns

explanation: Correct! Secondary prevention is all about early detection and screening so health issues can be caught and treated early. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h6)

question: When does a medication error cross the line from a civil mistake into criminal liability?

options.A: When the nurse's actions show reckless disregard for human life.
options.B: When the error results in an extended hospital stay.
options.C: When the patient complains loudly to the ward manager.
options.D: When the hospital management decides to issue a query.

explanation: Ordinary mistakes usually fall under civil negligence, but extreme recklessness that puts lives in grave danger crosses over into criminal territory. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h4)

question: Why might a nurse position an abdominal ultrasound patient to lie on their left side?

options.A: To stop them from rolling off the bed
options.B: To shift bowel gas away from the organs being checked
options.C: To boost their blood pressure for the Doppler scan
options.D: To relax their tummy muscles completely

explanation: Shifting the patient's position helps move pesky gas-filled loops of the bowel out of the way of the ultrasound beam. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h6)

question: What does the term 'cachexia' mean in advanced illness?

options.A: A sudden increase in daily appetite
options.B: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.C: An infection caused by poor dental hygiene
options.D: Severe muscle wasting and weight loss

explanation: You've got this! Cachexia is a whole-body wasting condition caused by disease inflammation, not just because the person isn't eating enough food. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h2)

question: How often should you flush a continuous feeding NG tube with water to keep it clear?

options.A: Immediately after every shift change
options.B: Every 4 to 6 hours
options.C: Only when the patient coughs
options.D: Once every 48 hours

explanation: Flushing every 4 to 6 hours keeps the formula from drying out and blocking the tube. Regular maintenance keeps things flowing smoothly! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T1#GNS212_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the best way to explain home care instructions to a patient with low health literacy?

options.A: Relying entirely on written pamphlets without verbal explanation
options.B: Using simple, plain language and asking the client to repeat instructions
options.C: Speaking in complex clinical terminology to sound professional
options.D: Handing the client a dense medical textbook to read overnight

explanation: You got it! Plain words plus the teach-back method (asking them to explain it back to you) guarantees they truly understand their treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is checking drug compatibility important when administering multiple intravenous infusions?

options.A: Incompatible drugs can react and form solid crystals that block the catheter
options.B: Combining medications changes the colour of the plastic infusion tubing
options.C: Mixing drugs always causes the patient to develop a skin rash
options.D: Incompatible solutions neutralize each other and make nurses look careless

explanation: Chemical reactions between mixed drugs can create precipitates that clog the line and endanger the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h6)

question: A nurse wants to study the shared daily habits and culture of nurses in a busy emergency room. Which research approach fits best?

options.A: Phenomenology
options.B: Grounded theory
options.C: Ethnography
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Brilliant! Ethnography is like diving into a specific cultural or social group to understand their shared workplace habits and lifestyle. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h3)

question: A patient presents with dry skin, flushed face, large pupils, and a racing heart after taking an unknown drug. Which toxidrome is this?

options.A: Sympathomimetic
options.B: Cholinergic
options.C: Opioid
options.D: Anticholinergic

explanation: Remember the fun medical rhyme for anticholinergic toxicity: 'blind as a bat, mad as a hatter, red as a beet, hot as a hare, dry as a bone!' [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: An oncology patient on chemotherapy develops a sudden fever of 38.8°C with no cough or sore spots. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Apply a warm compress to likely infection sites to check for tenderness
options.B: Encourage oral fluid intake and apply cold sponging to reduce the fever
options.C: Report the fever immediately and prepare for blood cultures and antibiotics
options.D: Recheck the temperature in four hours to see if it drops naturally

explanation: For a neutropenic patient, a fever is an emergency! Because they lack white blood cells to fight back, a small fever can turn into life-threatening sepsis very quickly. Always act fast. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which physical assessment step must a nurse ALWAYS do before pressing on a patient's abdomen?

options.A: Percussion
options.B: Palpation
options.C: Auscultation
options.D: Inspection

explanation: Awesome clinical thinking! Always listen with your stethoscope first so you don't accidentally alter natural bowel sounds by pressing on the tummy. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is actually happening inside the body during the incubation period of an infection?

options.A: The patient is experiencing the peak severity of organ inflammation
options.B: Body tissues are undergoing rapid repair after the infection clears
options.C: The immune system is actively clearing the pathogen from the blood
options.D: The pathogen is multiplying inside the host before symptoms appear

explanation: During the incubation period, the germ is quietly building up numbers inside the body. The patient feels completely fine—for now! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is it important to involve traditional leaders and birth attendants in community maternal health programs?

options.A: They provide financial loans to build local maternity clinics
options.B: They can legally perform emergency surgeries in villages
options.C: They help encourage early reporting of danger signs and prompt referral
options.D: They replace the need for professional midwives entirely

explanation: Spot on! Partnering with community influencers bridges traditional practices with modern healthcare, making sure mothers get to the clinic on time. Excellent perspective! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h8)

question: What is the main difference between vitamins and minerals?

options.A: Vitamins are organic compounds while minerals are inorganic elements.
options.B: Vitamins provide energy while minerals only regulate body temperature.
options.C: Minerals are required in large quantities while vitamins are trace elements.
options.D: Vitamins are synthesized by the body while minerals must be eaten.

explanation: Spot on! Vitamins are organic molecules (often acting as helpers called coenzymes), while minerals are inorganic elements from the earth and water that help with body structure and fluids. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h1)

question: Where do in-text citations usually go in a nursing paper?

options.A: At the very bottom of the page as small footnotes
options.B: Inside a separate appendix at the back of the book
options.C: Inside the body paragraphs near the borrowed information
options.D: Only on the title page beneath the student name

explanation: You've got this! In-text citations sit right inside your paragraphs to point readers to your sources instantly. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T7#GNS217_U3_T7_h3)

question: What sign should a nurse watch for as a delayed allergic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.B: Loss of taste on the tongue
options.C: Skin rash, hives, or itching
options.D: Temporary extra hair growth

explanation: Sometimes allergies show up hours later. Watch out for rashes, hives, or itching so you can treat them early. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of a soft diet?

options.A: To reduce chewing and digestion effort
options.B: To provide only liquid nutrients
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for teeth
options.D: To restrict all protein and fat intake

explanation: A soft diet is designed to be easy on the mouth, teeth, and stomach by requiring less mechanical chewing and digestive work. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h1)

question: Which check uses the mid-upper arm size to spot severe weight loss or wasting in children?

options.A: Clinical examination
options.B: Biochemical analysis
options.C: Body measurement (anthropometry)
options.D: Radiological imaging

explanation: Spot on! Anthropometry simply means taking body measurements like height, weight, and arm size to see how well a child is growing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why do we perform Leopold's maneuvers when a pregnant woman is admitted?

options.A: To determine the fetal position and presentation
options.B: To measure the mother's blood pressure accurately
options.C: To check if the amniotic fluid is clear or meconium-stained
options.D: To measure the exact cervical dilation in centimeters

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just our hands-on way of feeling the mum's tummy to figure out how the baby is lying inside. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing one's diet?

options.A: Cultural food traditions that conflict with medical diets
options.B: Possessing a strong personal desire to cook healthy meals
options.C: Lack of knowledge regarding food preparation skills
options.D: Financial constraints and the high cost of healthy food

explanation: Exactly! Wanting to cook healthy meals helps you succeed—it's a motivator, not a roadblock. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h5)

question: Why should nurses involve traditional and religious leaders when starting a new community health project?

options.A: They provide free medical supplies to the clinic
options.B: Their approval builds trust and community acceptance
options.C: They are trained to audit hospital financial records
options.D: They write all official government health policies

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. When they support a health initiative, the people are much more willing to listen and participate. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is a major risk when a patient takes herbal supplements along with their regular prescription drugs?

options.A: Herbs always neutralize all side effects of drugs
options.B: Adverse drug-nutrient or herb-drug interactions
options.C: The prescription drugs will become completely odorless
options.D: The medications will instantly turn into sugar

explanation: Herbs are active chemicals too! When mixed with hospital drugs, they can sometimes clash, making the drugs too strong or blocking them from working. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h5)

question: What is the main reason we calculate a patient's Body Mass Index (BMI)?

options.A: Determining daily fluid requirements
options.B: Screening for underweight, overweight, or obesity
options.C: Assessing cardiovascular fitness capacity
options.D: Measuring exact blood glucose levels

explanation: BMI is a quick way to use height and weight to check if a patient is carrying too much or too little weight. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h4)

question: What is the main job of counter-traction in a skeletal traction setup?

options.A: To double the amount of pulling force on the bone
options.B: To prevent the patient from sliding down and altering the pull
options.C: To keep the ropes from slipping out of the pulley grooves
options.D: To eliminate the need for regular pin site cleaning

explanation: Exactly! Counter-traction uses the patient's own body weight and gravity to pull in the opposite direction, keeping the traction steady and effective. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h2)

question: How does filtered bicarbonate cross the cell membrane of the kidney tubule?

options.A: It attaches to carrier proteins designed for glucose transport
options.B: It passes directly through large protein channels in the membrane
options.C: It converts to carbon dioxide and water before crossing
options.D: It is actively pumped across by specialized sodium carriers

explanation: Bicarbonate can't easily cross the membrane on its own because of its charge. So, it cleverly teams up with hydrogen to form gas and water first, which easily slip across! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T12#GNS121_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the blood clot that forms immediately after a bone breaks?

options.A: To permanently replace the broken bone
options.B: To stop all blood circulation to the limb
options.C: To provide a framework for incoming repair cells
options.D: To instantly turn into hard compact bone

explanation: The initial hematoma creates a stable matrix where specialized cells can migrate to begin building the healing tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a top priority at the bedside for a patient struggling with swallowing due to lower cranial nerve trouble?

options.A: Performing passive range of motion exercises on all extremities
options.B: Applying warm compresses to the forehead to relieve headache
options.C: Keeping mechanical suction equipment ready at the bedside
options.D: Encouraging a high-fiber diet to prevent constipation

explanation: You got this! Patients with trouble swallowing can easily choke or aspirate, so having suction ready keeps them safe. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T15#GNS211_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why is using frayed electrical cords dangerous?

options.A: They stop household light bulbs from working
options.B: Damaged cords pull too much electricity from the grid
options.C: Exposed wires can cause electric shock or fire
options.D: Frayed wires release toxic gases into the room

explanation: When insulation wears away, bare wires can spark against furniture or skin, causing burns or electrical shocks. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h7)

question: Where does a boat (or maritime) nurse primarily work?

options.A: Urban emergency dispatch response centers
options.B: Watercraft ranging from cruise liners to cargo ships
options.C: State-run land-based public health clinics
options.D: Specialized hospital intensive care units

explanation: Spot on! Boat nurses provide care right on the water aboard ships like cruise liners and cargo vessels, rather than working in standard land hospitals. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is a key daily responsibility of the nurse regarding barrier nursing?

options.A: Writing new infectious disease policies
options.B: Testing hospital water supplies daily
options.C: Ordering all hospital cleaning supplies
options.D: Ensuring proper compliance with infection control rules

explanation: Nurses must actively monitor and maintain infection control standards during every shift to protect patients and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: Which of the following is a direct health function of the PTA?

options.A: Stocking the school clinic with first aid materials
options.B: Performing surgical operations during emergencies
options.C: Prescribing antibiotics to sick students in class
options.D: Teaching all the mathematics lessons in school

explanation: Providing basic first aid supplies is a practical way the PTA helps manage minor health issues in school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h2)

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion has an intrauterine device (IUD) in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The IUD must be removed before the medications are administered
options.B: The dose of misoprostol should be doubled to compensate for the IUD
options.C: The IUD should only be removed if heavy bleeding starts
options.D: The patient can take mifepristone while the IUD remains inside

explanation: Safety first! The IUD has to come out before starting to prevent heavy bleeding or nasty pelvic infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h3)

question: You notice clear fluid leaking from a head dressing after a patient's craniotomy. What is this fluid likely to be?

options.A: Venous blood plasma only
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Topical wound ointment
options.D: Gastric acid secretions

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Clear or yellowish fluid leaking from a cranial site could be cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). This is an urgent finding that you must report to the surgeon right away. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why must a 24-hour emergency phone number be on hazardous material shipping documents?

options.A: To provide immediate expert guidance if a spill or exposure occurs
options.B: To let the receiving nurse ask about patient clinical history
options.C: To schedule the exact pickup time for the next laboratory batch
options.D: To allow the courier to confirm the payment receipt with accounting

explanation: If there's an accident on the road, emergency responders need someone to call instantly who knows how to handle that specific hazard safely. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h5)

question: As a nurse, which lab results are most helpful to check for a patient on a fat-restricted diet?

options.A: Serum cholesterol and triglycerides
options.B: White blood cell count and differential
options.C: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Coagulation times like PT and INR

explanation: Checking cholesterol and triglyceride levels lets you see directly how well the patient's body is handling fats. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h5)

question: A patient receiving neck radiation asks if they can use their favorite scented lotion on the area. What is the best reply?

options.A: Recommend using only approved, gentle, fragrance-free products to avoid further skin irritation
options.B: Suggest stopping all skin hygiene practices until the entire course of treatment finishes
options.C: Advise scrubbing the skin firmly with a washcloth before applying any cream or lotion
options.D: Encourage applying the scented lotion generously right before each radiation session

explanation: You're thinking like a caring nurse! Radiation makes skin very sensitive, so stick to mild, fragrance-free lotions approved by the care team. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is a biological vector?

options.A: A contaminated food supply that causes widespread food poisoning
options.B: An organism in which the pathogen multiplies or develops before infecting a human
options.C: A water pipe that carries treated municipal drinking water
options.D: A sterile surgical instrument used during sterile wound dressings

explanation: A biological vector is a living creature, like a mosquito, where the germ actually lives and grows part of its life cycle. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h5)

question: What is the main job of a bronchodilator in the airways?

options.A: Dissolving thick mucus plugs inside the bronchioles
options.B: Stopping the immune system from causing inflammation
options.C: Reducing bacterial infections in lung tissue
options.D: Relaxing bronchial smooth muscle to widen the airway

explanation: Bronchodilators help you breathe easier by relaxing the tight muscles around your airways, making them wider for air to pass through. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h1)

question: What type of data includes measurable physical signs and laboratory test results?

options.A: Objective data
options.B: Anecdotal data
options.C: Historical data
options.D: Subjective data

explanation: Objective data consists of observable and measurable facts gathered through physical examination and diagnostic testing. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is a bad practice that can cause tissue damage when giving injections?

options.A: Rotating sites when patients need repeated doses
options.B: Using the correct needle length for the patient's size
options.C: Giving multiple injections into the exact same spot
options.D: Allowing the skin disinfectant to dry before piercing

explanation: Spot on! Poking the exact same spot over and over causes hard, damaged tissue and scars. Always rotate your injection sites to give the skin and muscle a break! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h6)

question: What do we call a 'near miss' in the hospital?

options.A: An error that is caught before it reaches or harms the patient
options.B: A patient complaint about long waiting times at the clinic
options.C: A minor side effect of a drug that was expected by the doctor
options.D: An adverse event that causes permanent physical disability

explanation: Spot on! A near miss is a lucky save where a mistake almost happened, but someone caught it right on time before the patient got hurt. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h6)

question: What is the legal paper called that states a patient's treatment choices if they can no longer speak?

options.A: Nursing care plan
options.B: Discharge summary
options.C: Advance directive
options.D: Incident report

explanation: You've got it! An advance directive lets people put their medical wishes in writing beforehand so everyone knows what they want if they lose their voice. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h8)

question: What makes water a polar molecule?

options.A: An unequal sharing of electrical charge between hydrogen and oxygen atoms
options.B: A complete absence of chemical bonds between its constituent atoms
options.C: An equal balance of heavy metal ions dissolved in its liquid state
options.D: The presence of long carbon chains running through its core

explanation: The oxygen atom pulls electrons closer to itself, giving water a slightly negative side and a slightly positive hydrogen side. Clever design! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h7)

question: What does arterial bleeding typically look like?

options.A: Clear fluid mixed with streaks of old blood
options.B: Slowly oozing blood that stops without pressure
options.C: Bright red blood that spurts with each heartbeat
options.D: Dark red blood that flows in a steady stream

explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure straight from the heart, causing it to spurt when they are cut. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason for excluding a child from a nursery temporarily?

options.A: Persistent vomiting or unexplained severe diarrhea
options.B: A mild, clear runny nose without any fever or lethargy
options.C: An undiagnosed, contagious vesicular skin rash
options.D: A high fever accompanied by unusual lethargy

explanation: Mild upper respiratory symptoms like a clear runny nose without fever do not typically require exclusion, whereas contagious rashes, vomiting, and high fevers do. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main goal of modern patient safety design in healthcare?

options.A: To make doing the right thing easy and mistakes difficult
options.B: To eliminate all forms of human emotion from clinical work
options.C: To hide medical errors from patients and their families
options.D: To punish nurses severely whenever an adverse event occurs

explanation: Spot on! Good hospital design sets up simple workflows that naturally guide us to do the right thing every time. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h7)

question: How can mechanical ventilation affect a patient's blood circulation?

options.A: It has no effect on heart function
options.B: It increases the heart rate in every patient
options.C: It permanently damages heart muscle fibers
options.D: It alters chest pressures, which can impact blood flow

explanation: Because the machine pushes air into the chest using positive pressure, it changes the normal pressures inside. This can sometimes make it a bit harder for blood to return to the heart. Good to keep in mind at the bedside! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h1)

question: What are the two best ways to identify a patient before giving them medication?

options.A: Checking the ID band and asking their name and date of birth
options.B: Looking at the room number and asking the hospital cleaner
options.C: Checking the chart stored outside on the nurses' station desk
options.D: Recognizing their face from walking past their bed yesterday

explanation: Always use two unique identifiers—like checking their wristband and asking them to speak their name and DOB—to keep medication mix-ups away. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which criterion measures how many people in a population are affected by a health issue?

options.A: Magnitude
options.B: Confidentiality
options.C: Severity
options.D: Affordability

question: What is the main sign of psychosis in a patient?

question: How should a nurse approach dietary counselling with a patient?

question: Why can taking NSAIDs frequently lead to stomach ulcers?

question: What causes the blood vessels in a newborn's lungs to relax and open up at birth?

question: What must you do if an unsterile object accidentally touches your sterile field while setting up?

question: As a nurse, why should you immediately report even minor spotting in a postmenopausal woman?

question: In a primary hyposecretion problem, what do you expect the brain's tropic hormone levels to do?

question: Why is active pelvic inflammatory disease considered a strong contraindication for immediate MVA?

question: Why are gentle, early movements introduced after the initial swelling of a sprain goes down?

question: Why might a patient give a vague, unbelievable story about a bad injury during a home visit?

question: A patient is prescribed an inhaled bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid. In what order should they take them?

question: Which of these is a common sign of psychological trauma in a displaced child?

question: What does your body do with extra carbohydrates when you eat more than you immediately need?

question: Why must a nurse assess a patient's breathing technique and coordination before handing them an inhaler?

question: How does teaching a new family during postnatal home visits help them?

question: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), how is health best defined today?

question: What action should a nurse take when a fiberglass measuring tape starts to show stretched markings?

question: A mother is worried because her 9-month-old baby is not walking yet. What should you tell her?

question: What factor most heavily influences how well a newborn with a birth defect will recover?

question: Which group of blood pressure medications must be strictly avoided during pregnancy because they can harm the baby's kidneys?

question: A patient decides to stay in an abusive home for a little longer while sorting out resources. What should the nurse do?

question: What is the main legal reason why patient health records must be accurate and timely?

question: A mum at 28 weeks comes to the clinic with swollen face and high blood pressure. What should the nurse suspect?

question: When is the best time to start palliative care for someone with a serious illness?

question: What is the main reason a patient's serum bilirubin level shoots up?

question: Why is creating a warm, non-judgmental environment so essential in family planning nursing?

options.C: To shorten the total amount of time needed for data collection
options.D: To help the participant feel comfortable and build trust

explanation: Starting with gentle, straightforward questions eases anxiety and encourages people to complete the rest of the questionnaire. Brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why is looking at community data just as important for a nurse as giving bedside care?

options.A: Clinical procedures are secondary to statistical data collection
options.B: Patients refuse care unless statistics are explained first
options.C: Data helps identify community service gaps and allocate resources
options.D: Hospitals require nurses to publish annual demographic research

explanation: Bedside care is vital, but looking at the big picture data helps us find villages or groups who are missing out on care so we can send help where it's needed most! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T027#GNS226_U6_T027_h1)

question: Roughly what percentage of whole blood is made up of plasma?

options.A: About 55 percent
options.B: About 90 percent
options.C: About 25 percent
options.D: About 75 percent

explanation: Spot on! Plasma is the straw-colored liquid part of your blood, making up just over half (about 55%) of your total blood volume. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which member of the healthcare team helps a patient relearn how to swallow safely?

options.A: Clinical Pharmacist
options.B: Physical Therapist
options.C: Speech-Language Pathologist
options.D: Occupational Therapist

explanation: Well done! Speech-Language Pathologists do much more than speech—they are experts in evaluating and treating swallowing difficulties too. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h3)

question: How do specialized support cohorts differ from standard general groups?

options.A: They focus on the unique life challenges of specific populations like adolescents or pregnant women.
options.B: They require mandatory financial contributions from every attending member.
options.C: They meet exclusively inside high-security hospital surgical wards.
options.D: They exclude anyone who has been on antiretroviral medication for more than one year.

explanation: Specialized cohorts target specific groups so members can discuss challenges unique to their life stage or medical condition. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: What is the big benefit of using an inhaler instead of pills for an asthma patient?

options.A: It works within seconds to stop sudden bronchial muscle spasms completely
options.B: It delivers medication directly to lung tissue and reduces systemic side effects
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of developing oral fungal infections
options.D: It bypasses the liver entirely so the drug never enters the bloodstream

explanation: Inhalers send the drug right where the trouble is (the lungs), meaning less medicine floats around the rest of the body causing side effects. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h4)

question: Why are ACE inhibitors or ARBs frequently prescribed for nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: They prevent bacterial infections in the urinary tract
options.B: They completely cure the underlying autoimmune disease
options.C: They replace lost albumin directly in the bloodstream
options.D: They decrease pressure inside the glomerulus to reduce protein leakage

explanation: These medications relax the tiny blood vessels leaving the glomerulus, lowering the pressure that forces protein out into the urine. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h4)

question: How should you position an adult patient's pinna to straighten their ear canal before looking inside?

options.A: Upward and forward
options.B: Straight down
options.C: Upward and backward
options.D: Downward and forward

explanation: For adults, pulling the pinna upward and backward straightens out that natural S-curve of the ear canal so you can see clearly. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main clue that tells you a patient has Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) rather than regular stress?

options.A: The patient experiences complete memory loss during stressful events.
options.B: The symptoms only appear when the person is exposed to bright lights.
options.C: The physical symptoms include high fever and joint stiffness.
options.D: The worry is chronic, excessive, and lasts for at least six months.

explanation: With GAD, the constant heavy worry doesn't just pass in a week—it sticks around for six months or more, covering practically everything. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the main thing you do during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Gathering initial demographic data during the patient's admission
options.B: Writing out shift handoff notes without checking patient progress
options.C: Comparing the patient's actual health status against the expected outcomes
options.D: Formulating brand new medical diagnoses for the physician to sign

explanation: Evaluation is like checking your scorecard. You look back at the goals you set and ask, 'Did our care help the patient reach them?' [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why might a nurse or doctor collect a vulval tissue biopsy during an investigation?

options.A: To flush out trapped bacteria from the urinary bladder
options.B: To test the patency of the fallopian tubes
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels in the bloodstream
options.D: To check for chronic skin conditions or rule out abnormal cell changes

explanation: A biopsy sounds scary, but it's just a way for the lab to take a closer look at skin cells under a microscope when standard treatments aren't working. You're mastering diagnostic steps! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h4)

question: Right after finishing a sterile dressing change, what final detail should you write on the dressing tape?

options.A: The hospital's insurance billing code.
options.B: The date, time, and your initials.
options.C: The patient's diagnosis and room number.
options.D: A friendly smiley face for the patient.

explanation: Labeling your work lets the rest of the healthcare team know exactly when the dressing was changed and who did it. Professional habit unlocked! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h6)
